title: The library that burned slowly
text: The Great Library of Alexandria {{1}} founded at the start of the third century BC {{2}} the Greek-speaking kings of Egypt, {{3}} ambition was to collect every significant scroll in the known world. Ancient writers claimed {{4}} the shelves eventually held hundreds of thousands of rolls, and visiting ships {{5}} reportedly searched so that any new book could be copied before the original was returned. The library declined over centuries, and {{6}} exactly it ended — fire, funding cuts or slow decay — is still debated, yet the institution mattered {{7}} for its building than for what happened inside: scholars there measured the Earth's circumference, mapped the stars and edited Homer. {{8}} was, in effect, the first great research institute, and the idea of such a place may be its most durable legacy.
